brief: Banking app with no monthly fees and early direct deposit. Mainly younger and mid-income Americans, with a goal of account signups. Needs to comply with financial advertising rules.

profile.business_summary: A mobile banking app offering early direct deposit and no monthly fees, targeting younger and mid-income Americans with the goal of driving new account signups under financial advertising compliance.

relevant_tags.why: Younger, mid-income consumers seeking no-fee banking highly value digital convenience.
Digitally native DTC shoppers are comfortable adopting mobile-first financial services.
While free, a banking app represents an ongoing, continuous relationship similar to a digital subscription.

config.advertiser_summary: A mobile banking app offering early direct deposit and no monthly fees, targeting younger and mid-income Americans with the goal of driving new account signups under financial advertising compliance.

assumptions: Price not given; assumed $25 for a 'budget' product.
No target CPA/ROAS or margin given; assumed 30% gross margin (typical for instant_delivery). Give a target CPA to replace this.
Target CPA = 70% of max affordable CAC ($25 x 30% margin x 1.3 orders = $9.75).

pricing.rationale: Acquisition goal with no conversion history: pay per click. Max CPC = target CPA $6.82 x click-to-purchase rate (1.3%-4.6% for instant_delivery). Clicks are observable without trusting a pixel, so both sides can verify billing.
pricing.tcpa_unlock: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded; until then Disco can't predict conversion rate for this brand.

budget.pacing: even daily pacing; pause a host if CPA > 2.0x target after 150 clicks

allocations.rationale: score 0.29 -> relative fit x1.40 on CTR/CVR; max bid $0.25 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%

warnings: No budget given: recommending $90, the smallest budget that buys 300 clicks per host.

phases.name: learning
phases.rule: bid = start bid per host (70% of break-even); pacing adjustment only
phases.why: stable bids so measured CTR/CVR aren't confounded by bid changes

phases.name: enhanced_cpc
phases.until: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded; until then Disco can't predict conversion rate for this brand.
phases.rule: bid = start bid x conversion_likelihood x pacing, clamped to [floor, max bid]
phases.why: spend more on shoppers who look likely to buy, never above break-even

phases.name: target_cpa
phases.rule: Disco bids automatically to hit $6.82 CPA
phases.why: only once Disco can predict this brand's conversion rate

adjustments.reason: Bid higher when the shopper looks like a high converter: their persona match for this campaign vs the host's average shopper (from the serve-time persona posterior).
Under-delivering vs the daily plan -> bid up a little; over-delivering -> bid down.

bid_strategy.rationale: Start below break-even and fixed so the first two weeks measure the hosts, not the bidder; then bid per shopper within a hard ceiling (max CPC = target CPA x CVR), so a single click can never cost more than it's expected to earn.
